title: set --status changes the field without moving the slice file

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`ops.set_fields` is a plain `setattr` loop, so `slicer set S01 --status done` writes the
new status onto the item and stops there. `ops.set_status` is the one that moves the
slice file across the `slices/` → `slices/done/` boundary, and `set` never calls it.

The result is silent state corruption: the index says done, the file is still in the open
folder, and `slicer verify` reports `slice file is in the wrong folder for status`. The
user did nothing wrong and gets no warning at the time.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `Set_StatusToDone_MovesTheSliceFile` — set a status that crosses the boundary,
   assert the file moved and `verify` is clean.
2. `Set_StatusUnchanged_DoesNotTouchTheFile`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Relocation moved out of `set_status` into `_relocate_slice`, which moves the file and
logs nothing. `set_status` calls it and keeps writing its own `status` entry, so `done`,
`park` and `unpark` are unchanged. `set_fields` calls it when the status actually
changed. `retire` had the same move dance inline and now shares the one path too — the
point of this slice is that exactly one function knows the folder mapping.

**The log decision:** one entry, not two. A combined `set --status done --size M` writes
a single `set` entry whose `note` names both fields and whose `from`/`to` carry the
transition, so nothing is lost by not also writing a `status` record:

    2026-09-24T20:04:43Z  S01   set      open -> done  status

**Not in this slice:** reconciling the other duplicated index/slice fields; that is S08.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `slicer verify` clean after a `set --status` round trip.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit. `ops.py` and the tests that pin the new behaviour.
